findings.body:
**Claimed critical; verifier found:** verifier off

Removing the `ALLOWED_HOSTS` check makes `deliver()` issue a server-side POST to any caller-supplied `url`. A customer- or attacker-controlled value such as `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` or `http://127.0.0.1:2375/` is fetched from the application/runtime network with no host, scheme, or private-IP validation.

Restore an egress policy before merging: HTTPS-only, resolve and reject loopback/link-local/private/metadata ranges (and DNS rebinding), and keep a configurable allowlist or equivalent per-tenant destination policy. A bare `urlopen` on untrusted input is not safe for multi-tenant webhook delivery.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change removes the only host allowlist on outbound webhook delivery and turns `deliver()` into an open SSRF primitive.

## Analysis

`webhooks.py` previously restricted destinations to `ALLOWED_HOSTS` (`hooks.internal.example`) before `urllib.request.urlopen`. The PR deletes that check and posts to whatever `url` the caller supplies, with only a 5s timeout left as protection.

Any caller that passes a customer- or attacker-controlled URL can hit:
- cloud metadata (`169.254.169.254`), link-local, and RFC1918 hosts
- localhost / sidecar admin ports on the runner or app network
- non-HTTP schemes `urllib` will follow, depending on handler registration

Supporting customer webhook endpoints is a valid product goal, but it needs an explicit egress policy (HTTPS-only, DNS rebinding-safe IP checks, block private/link-local/metadata ranges, optional per-tenant allowlist), not deletion of the existing gate.

## Release decision

**Recommendation:** request-changes
